Subject: Estate Inventory and Valuation Process
Body:
Hi Jenny,

I am a Duke Student and am reaching out due to your expertise in estate planning.

I am researching a specific bottleneck in Trust administration: the time spent manually inventorying and valuing physical household assets (vehicles, furniture, "contents").

I’m developing a workflow tool designed to act as a triage system for estates:

*        Automate the "Noise": Instantly catalogs and prices standard items (using KBB/market data) to clear the backlog.

*        Flag the Wealth: Automatically identifies high-value assets (Real Estate, Fine Art) to route to your certified appraisers.

The goal is to eliminate the administrative grunt work for your Trust Officers without compromising your liability protection on high-value items.

Is the physical inventory process currently a time-sink for your team, or have you found a way to automate it?

Best,

Graham Mills

Body:

My passion for the investment process was solidified at Willow Hill Capital and Novant Health. 	Reviewing SEC filings and transcripts.

	Generating answers with exact citations back to the source docs.

Subject: Student Offering to Help with Your Inbox
Body:
Hi T,
My name is Graham, and I'm a student at Duke University.
While working part-time at a disease nonprofit alongside my studies, I noticed how often people reach out to organizations through contact forms and general inboxes without ever hearing back. Many of these messages come from individuals seeking help or support during difficult times, and it's hard to imagine their words going unread.
I know inboxes can pile up quickly, especially for organizations doing meaningful work, so if responding to every message has become a challenge, I'd be glad to lend a hand. As a student with the time and care to dedicate to this, I'm offering to monitor and respond to your inbox at no cost to your organization, so that every person who reaches out gets a reply.
If this sounds like something that could be a good fit, I'd love to set up a quick chat to share more. And if your organization doesn't need this kind of support, I'd be grateful if you could point me toward any others in your network who might.
Thank you for your time, and I look forward to hearing from you.
Best,
Graham

*	Pay the $500 non-refundable deposit that goes towards your overall program fees. Instructions to pay the deposit payment on your IFSA Portal can be found here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fifsa.my.salesforce.com%2Fsfc%2Fp%2F%2361000000Hzj3%2Fa%2F4N000000Rg04%2Fb_ev_HG93YVxj_Do3AiLAVoOrh0WlXpnsK0O1zENKh0&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C3234eee25b92434d68fa08de9be566f2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639119606757238579%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=lHRLCRDcBdI1mEnmvkOU%2BYZfoEq2AdQ2AWpy5uVEds8%3D&reserved=0> . 

 

You can find the above items in your IFSA Portal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fifsa.my.site.com%2FIFSAStudentPortal%2Flogin&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C3234eee25b92434d68fa08de9be566f2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639119606757278765%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=v4nQQFNOmnd1UXvYARWcPqHpemb0F0rTQboFG9CifXI%3D&reserved=0> .

Please be sure to read over the following information in this email carefully:

Subject: Academic Planning & Part-Time Status for Fall 2027
Body:
Dear Dean Bruno,
I hope this email finds you well! I am a current sophomore studying in the Duke in New York program this semester, and you are listed as my Academic Dean for Trinity College.
I am reaching out because I need to make a strategic adjustment to my graduation timeline. I am planning to graduate in December 2027 (7 semesters, continuously enrolled). This timeline aligns with both my academic pacing and the recruiting cycle for a finance internship I am targeting, which follows a "Class of 2028" timeline.
To align with this without overloading my schedule, I plan to stay continuously enrolled for 7 semesters (no leave of absence) and pace my final requirements. Based on my review of Trinity policies, my plan is to:
Apply 8 of my AP credits toward my 34-credit graduation requirement, utilizing the continuous enrollment policy.
Complete my remaining Economics B.S. core requirements (ECON 204 and ECON 301) during my Junior year to bypass the senior-year core restriction.
Carry my remaining 1.5 to 2.0 credits into my 7th and final semester (Fall 2027) and apply for Part-Time Degree-Seeking Status.
I have run a "What-If" report in Stellic mapping out my next three semesters, and it shows all Trinity and Economics B.S. requirements turning green by December 2027 under this exact plan.
Because this involves AP credit retention and future part-time status approval, I want to ensure I haven't missed any hidden roadblocks. I am also on a bit of a time-sensitive deadline — I have a study abroad deposit due within the next five days for Fall 2025, and whether part-time status in Fall 2027 is viable directly impacts whether I pursue that program or take a different path. If you are able to weigh in over email, that would be incredibly helpful — but I am also happy to jump on a brief Zoom call if that's easier.
Thank you so much for your time and guidance.
Best regards,
Graham Mills

Subject: Interinstitutional Course Approval Request
Body:
Dear Professor Fullenkamp,
I hope this email finds you well. I am a Duke undergraduate currently studying abroad, and I am in the process of finalizing my course schedule for my return to Durham in Fall 2026.
I am hoping to take an interinstitutional course at NC State that will count toward my Economics/Financial Economics (FEcon) elective requirements. I have found three potential courses and have attached their syllabi to this email. Because undergraduates can only take one interinstitutional course per semester, I have ranked them in my order of preference:

1.	
	Top Choice: BUS 474: Logistics Management
2.	
	First Backup: BUS 458: Analytics: Data to Decisions
3.	
	Second Backup: BUS 470: Business Process Management

Could you please review my top choice (BUS 474) to see if it would be approved specifically as an Econ/FEcon elective? If it is not a match, I would greatly appreciate it if you could evaluate the backups.
I have also attached a partially filled Interinstitutional Approval Form. Once we confirm which course is approved, I would appreciate your digital signature on the form so I can route it to my Academic Dean.
Thank you so much for your time and consideration.
Best,
Graham Mills

	Hello,

	Thank you for your interest in the 'AI Solutions Analyst' position. Before continuing, we had a technical question regarding your response. This question aims to better understand your expertise in the AI implementation space.

	Project Overview: Architecting an Autonomous Market Intelligence System
	We are looking to move beyond manual data research by building a sophisticated Multi-Agent AI System. Our business centers on developing high-quality contact and data networks for leadership gatherings, capturing the complete market ecosystem for major cities - including top developers, architects, and city planners. Currently, this process involves manual LinkedIn searching and Excel management; we want to replace this with an automated, "agentic" pipeline.
	
	The goal is to develop an AI framework where specialized agents work independently or via API-linked swarms. The first phase involves Geospatial Intelligence: agents will scrape Google Maps for city addresses and autonomously classify buildings as residential, commercial, or non-profit. This creates the foundational layer of our digital map, identifying the physical makeup of a target market without human intervention.
	
	Once a building is identified, the system will trigger a "Deep Research" workflow. Using frameworks like LangGraph or CrewAI, secondary agents will cross-reference these addresses against real estate databases like LoopNet and public records. The objective is to trace the "DNA" of a property - identifying building owners, majority/minor partners, and institutional funders - effectively mapping the financial and professional web behind every structure.
	
	To ensure data integrity, we are implementing a "Scaffolding" architecture. This means utilizing a "Manager Agent" to verify findings through a chain-of-consensus, checking information across multiple sources to eliminate hallucinations. We are looking for someone who can transition us from static spreadsheets to a dynamic, self-correcting Knowledge Graph that automates the entire Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) process.

	To move forward, please outline your proposed technical solution. Specifically, we’d like to see a detailed step-by-step roadmap of how you would architect this project from the initial geospatial scraping to the multi-agent verification layer. Please clarify where you would utilize hard-coded logic versus where you would lean on agentic orchestration (like LangChain or CrewAI) to achieve the most reliable results or whether, you would pursue something else entirely.

	Hello,

	Thank you for your interest in the 'AI Solutions Analyst' position. Before continuing, we had a technical question regarding your response. This question aims to better understand your expertise in the AI implementation space.

	Project Overview: Architecting an Autonomous Market Intelligence System
	We are looking to move beyond manual data research by building a sophisticated Multi-Agent AI System. Our business centers on developing high-quality contact and data networks for leadership gatherings, capturing the complete market ecosystem for major cities - including top developers, architects, and city planners. Currently, this process involves manual LinkedIn searching and Excel management; we want to replace this with an automated, "agentic" pipeline.
	
	The goal is to develop an AI framework where specialized agents work independently or via API-linked swarms. The first phase involves Geospatial Intelligence: agents will scrape Google Maps for city addresses and autonomously classify buildings as residential, commercial, or non-profit. This creates the foundational layer of our digital map, identifying the physical makeup of a target market without human intervention.
	
	Once a building is identified, the system will trigger a "Deep Research" workflow. Using frameworks like LangGraph or CrewAI, secondary agents will cross-reference these addresses against real estate databases like LoopNet and public records. The objective is to trace the "DNA" of a property - identifying building owners, majority/minor partners, and institutional funders - effectively mapping the financial and professional web behind every structure.
	
	To ensure data integrity, we are implementing a "Scaffolding" architecture. This means utilizing a "Manager Agent" to verify findings through a chain-of-consensus, checking information across multiple sources to eliminate hallucinations. We are looking for someone who can transition us from static spreadsheets to a dynamic, self-correcting Knowledge Graph that automates the entire Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) process.

	To move forward, please outline your proposed technical solution. Specifically, we’d like to see a detailed step-by-step roadmap of how you would architect this project from the initial geospatial scraping to the multi-agent verification layer. Hello,

Thank you for your interest in the 'AI Solutions Analyst' position. Before continuing, we had a technical question regarding your response. This question aims to better understand your expertise in the AI implementation space.

Project Overview: Architecting an Autonomous Market Intelligence System
We are looking to move beyond manual data research by building a sophisticated Multi-Agent AI System. Our business centers on developing high-quality contact and data networks for leadership gatherings, capturing the complete market ecosystem for major cities - including top developers, architects, and city planners. Currently, this process involves manual LinkedIn searching and Excel management; we want to replace this with an automated, "agentic" pipeline.

The goal is to develop an AI framework where specialized agents work independently or via API-linked swarms. The first phase involves Geospatial Intelligence: agents will scrape Google Maps for city addresses and autonomously classify buildings as residential, commercial, or non-profit. This creates the foundational layer of our digital map, identifying the physical makeup of a target market without human intervention.

Once a building is identified, the system will trigger a "Deep Research" workflow. Using frameworks like LangGraph or CrewAI, secondary agents will cross-reference these addresses against real estate databases like LoopNet and public records. The objective is to trace the "DNA" of a property - identifying building owners, majority/minor partners, and institutional funders - effectively mapping the financial and professional web behind every structure.

To ensure data integrity, we are implementing a "Scaffolding" architecture. This means utilizing a "Manager Agent" to verify findings through a chain-of-consensus, checking information across multiple sources to eliminate hallucinations. We are looking for someone who can transition us from static spreadsheets to a dynamic, self-correcting Knowledge Graph that automates the entire Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) process.

To move forward, please outline your proposed technical solution. Specifically, we’d like to see a detailed step-by-step roadmap of how you would architect this project from the initial geospatial scraping to the multi-agent verification layer. Please clarify where you would utilize hard-coded logic versus where you would lean on agentic orchestration (like LangChain or CrewAI) to achieve the most reliable results or whether, you would pursue something else entirely.

We’d like to know what you’d aim to get out of the internship and how your skills and background would translate to the tasks listed below.

 

These responsibilities are an indication of the internship tasks and are non-exhaustive. Internships will be fully virtual, and interns will receive an hourly wage equivalent to the minimum wage.

 

Investment Internship

*	Live deal work
*	Build models
*	Participate in investment diligence
*	Create investor and lender materials
*	Support investment memo creation
*	Build law firm profiles
*	Help sourcing process
*	Send cold emails and make cold phone calls
*	Run fund-level analyses
*	Support fundraising process

 

Marketing Internship

*	Create LEA thought pieces
*	Manage LEA social media pages
*	Create LEA marketing materials
*	Help portfolio companies create marketing campaigns
*	Manage portfolio company marketing campaigns
*	Create portfolio company marketing materials
*	Assess law firm brand strength, across portfolio companies and potential investments
*	Create marketing strategies as part of investment process
*	Run return on ad spend analyses
*	Conduct competitive analysis across markets
*	Test new acquisition channels (TikTok, YouTube, local partnerships)
*	Support retargeting and CRM-driven marketing strategies
*	Help localize campaigns for new geographic expansions

 

Operations Internship (May Be Split Into Separate Operations vs. Technology Internships)

*	Institute reporting packages
*	Analyze portfolio company value creation opportunities
*	Implement value creation opportunities, including geographic expansion, hiring initiatives, referral network buildouts, real estate asset sales
*	Help implement technology, including employee training
*	Help form partnerships with leading legal vendors
*	Map out portfolio company intake process
*	Develop intakes scripts for best practices
*	Help portfolio company hiring needs
*	Establish portfolio-wide benchmarking
*	Support fundraising process
*	May require travel to portfolio companies
*	Apply various data science methods to create tools for LEA to maximize its investment efficiency and for portfolio companies to implement technology
*	Create an LEA CRM

*	Analyze and recommend best Legal Tech tools

Hi Graham - thanks for reaching out. To be honest, it's a little bit hard to gauge how to give you advice here because I don't know the firm or their investment strategy, nor do I have a sense for the industries these companies are in. My advice would be to pick the company that you think aligns more closely to the firm's investment strategy, then flag the key considerations that are giving you pause and address those in the diligence questions. To be honest, investing is very subjective. An exercise like this likely doesn't have a "right" answer; rather, it's meant to test your ability to think like an investor. In this job, when you make any investment, hopefully, you've done enough diligence to understand how to price risk, but ultimately, you won't know whether you're right until the business exits. 

On the format, a simple memo in a word document should suffice. You should probably include an exec summary paragraph at the beginning including what you need to believe for this investment to work, investment merits and growth opportunities, then the section on diligence considerations. I would also include ways you think you can address those diligence considerations (e.g., what data requests you'd make, etc.).
